text.title: Claude Code Headless Default — Worked Examples
text.summary: The `claude -p` invocation pattern that orchestrators should standardise on for non-interactive runs. Also a quickcheck of the CLI-vs-SDK decision on one task.

example.title: Coding task, no trigger — CLI
example.code: Task: "fix flaky test in tests/test_auth.py" Domain? coding ✓ Triggers? none ✓ → use `claude -p` (CLI default)
example.note: Coding task, no SDK trigger fired — CLI is correct.

example.title: Same task, hand-rolled SDK loop
example.code: Task: "fix flaky test in tests/test_auth.py" Decision: write a 400-line Python loop using anthropic.Anthropic() calling tools manually.
example.note: Re-implements file/edit/bash/git tools that the CLI already ships. No SDK trigger justifies this.

section.title: Good vs bad invocation

example.title: Canonical headless argv
example.code: claude -p "Fix failing test in tests/test_auth.py" \ --output-format stream-json --verbose \ --allowedTools "Read,Edit,Bash(pytest:*)" \ --max-turns 20 \ < /dev/null
example.note: Explicit allowlist, capped turns, closed stdin, stream-json output for orchestrator events.

example.title: Unbounded invocation
example.note: No allowlist, no turn cap, no stream-json — the orchestrator cannot react to mid-run events and tool access is unbounded.

section.note: `templates/run-headless.sh`: Reference wrapper that wires every required flag and budget logic.
See also `../stream-json-orchestration/AGENTS.md`: How to drive an orchestrator state-machine off stream-json events.
